speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: It is part of the Kampung Admiralty development, a greenfield Housing and Development Board (HDB) project which I initiated in 2012 when I was in the Ministry of National Development.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The project site was a vacant plot of 9,800 square metres (m2) – almost 10,000 m2 – next to Admiralty MRT station where HDB had planned to build 2-room Studio Apartments for seniors.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: We decided to intensify the land use to meet the diverse needs of the potential residential and commercial tenants.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: I appointed a committee and while the primary objective was to build Studio Apartments for the seniors, I advised the committee to identify the daily needs of the seniors, beyond mere accommodation, so that the seniors could access such needs easily and with little hassle.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: I envisaged Kampung Admiralty to be a mixed precinct that our seniors would find highly liveable and where neighbours look out for one another, with the good old kampung spirit.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: And that is why we named the project "Kampung Admiralty", to help focus the planning.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The committee surveyed the needs of the residents in the precinct and sought the views of the many commuters who regularly used Admiralty MRT station.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Over several months, they conducted extensive public consultations and organised many focus group discussions with the potential users of this project.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Out of a long wish list, the committee finally decided on the range of services to be provided.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: These included a hawker centre, an outpatient medical-cum-day surgery centre, a childcare centre, an elderly day care centre, some commercial spaces for shops and restaurants.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: All these were built, in addition to the Studio Apartments for the elderly, as per the original intent of this project.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: We also made generous provisions for greenery and public spaces to support community gardening, so that the elderly residents living there could live an active lifestyle.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: We also wanted to make this precinct user-friendly for the many residents who cycle to Admiralty MRT station.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: There were many surface bicycle parking lots at Admiralty MRT station, but they were not enough during peak hours.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The shortage was serious back then, with indiscriminately parked bicycles cluttering the parking area and posing safety concerns.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The committee did several counts of the parked bicycles there.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: They projected substantial, long-term demand for over 500 cycling lots in the vicinity of Admiralty MRT station and proposed to meet the demand as part of the Kampung Admiralty project.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: We then had to choose between surface parking or underground parking.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Surface parking was cheaper to build, but underground parking would free up valuable surface space for other uses; and this is an important consideration in land-scarce Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: As Japan faces similar land constraints, the committee studied their experience with bicycle parking and became aware of the extensive underground bicycle parking facilities in their cities.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) made study visits to Japan to find out more.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: I myself visited similar facilities in Tokyo when I happened to be there on one official visit.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Each facility stored up to 200 bicycles and charged users up to S$35 a month – so, about a dollar per day – for usage of bicycle parking services.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: My impression was that the Japanese were very satisfied with their paid underground facilities.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: After much deliberation, the committee decided to experiment with underground bicycle parking in Kampung Admiralty, to see if this model could be financially viable in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: HDB called an open tender for the construction of the entire Kampung Admiralty in 2014 and received six competitive bids.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: HDB eventually awarded the contract to Lum Chang Building Contractors, which subcontracted the construction, maintenance and operation of the bicycle parking system to a Spanish company, which met the relevant requirements.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The Kampung Admiralty project was completed in 2017.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The final plot ratio is 3.6, in line with our intent to intensify land use.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: We set aside 198 m2 – so, that is about 2,000 square feet – for underground bicycle lots, adjacent to the much larger basement car park of about 12,400 m2.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: So, the bicycle parking lot is less than 2% of the total underground parking space.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: While Kampung Admiralty was being built, the shared dockless bicycle phenomenon popped up in Singapore!

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Remember the very colourful Ofo, oBike shared bicycles?

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: We were surprised by the rapid public acceptance and growth of shared bicycles, which led to many problems.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: By then, I had moved to the Ministry of Transport (MOT) and had to deal with it, including imposing regulatory controls on the operators.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: But just as we managed down the shared bicycle numbers, e-scooters came along.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The new devices had many advantages and took off quickly, creating new problems which we are now actively dealing with.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: In fact, two Bills are coming up in an hour's time to deal with this problem.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Both shared bicycles and personal mobility devices (PMDs), especially e-scooters, have dramatically shifted the usage and parking patterns of privately owned bicycles.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: This fundamentally altered the economics of paid underground bicycle parking.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The underground space of 198 m2 for bicycle parking remains, and can be repurposed.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: We are keeping the options open, as the current situation is still changing.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: I think what it highlights is the difficulty of forecasting demand during market research.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: So, it will be very useful if the Ministry could put in place guidelines for market research studies, even a logic model that has to take place before these projects proceed.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: And the idea is, after the project commences, we can check back against these original projections and see where did we go wrong, where did we go right.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: That will be very useful because it is only now that we are hearing this very excellent story of what actually happened.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: But for this particular episode, it is an ongoing saga.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: We cannot tell yet how the saga will end; perhaps, in a couple of years' time.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I personally think that demand for privately owned bicycles phenomenon may grow, especially as we expand the cycling path infrastructure, a topic which we will discuss extensively at next month's Committee of Supply for MOT.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
